title: Provide feed and nutrition for poultry

lessons.title: What poultry need to eat
lessons.html:
What poultry need to eat

Chickens grow and lay eggs from the feed they eat. Good feed, given the right way, keeps birds healthy and makes money for the farm.

What is in the feed

  • Energy comes mostly from maize. It gives birds power to move, keep warm and grow.
  • Protein comes from soya and other meals. It builds muscle, feathers and eggs.
  • Minerals like calcium make strong bones and egg shells.
  • Vitamins keep birds healthy.
  • Water is not in the bag, but birds need clean water all the time.

Different feeds for different birds

Birds need different feed at different ages. The feed mill makes each feed for one stage.

BirdExample feeds
Broilers (meat chickens)Starter, grower, finisher
Young layers (pullets)Chick starter, grower, developer
Laying hensLayer feed with extra calcium

Always read the bag label. Give each group of birds only the feed your supervisor tells you. Wrong feed can make birds sick or stop them laying.

Feed forms

Feed comes as mash (powder), crumbles (small pieces) or pellets. Small chicks usually get crumbles. Older birds may get pellets or mash.

Never feed

  • Mouldy, wet or caked feed.
  • Feed that smells bad.
  • Feed from a torn bag that rats have been in.
  • Feed made for other animals, unless your supervisor says so.

Mouldy feed can contain poisons that harm birds and lower growth and egg numbers.

Grit and shell

Some farms give layers extra limestone grit or oyster shell for strong shells. Give it only if your supervisor tells you, and in the amount you are shown. Too much calcium for young birds can harm their kidneys.

lessons.title: Feeding birds and storing feed
lessons.html:
Feeding birds and storing feed

Filling feeders

  1. Check the feeders on every round.
  2. Set the feeder height so the lip of the pan or trough is about level with the birds' backs. Raise it as the birds grow.
  3. Fill feeders so birds can eat but do not throw feed out. Wasted feed on the floor is wasted money.
  4. Make sure there is enough feeder space so all birds can eat at the same time.
  5. Check that automatic feed lines run to the end of the house.
  6. Clean out wet or caked feed from pans.

Storing feed

  • Keep bags on pallets, off the floor and away from the walls.
  • Keep the store dry, cool and closed to rats, birds and wild animals.
  • Use old feed first: first in, first out.
  • Close silo lids so rain cannot get in.
  • Keep chemicals, poisons and fuel away from feed.

Safety

Feed bags are heavy, often 40 or 50 kg. Bend your knees, keep your back straight and ask for help with heavy loads. Never climb into a silo. Feed can move and bury you. Only trained people with the right safety plan may enter a silo. Wear a dust mask when you handle dusty feed.

Records

Write down how much feed each house used each day and the feed type. If the birds eat much less than usual, tell your supervisor at once. Sick birds eat less.

Key points

  • Feed gives energy, protein, minerals and vitamins.
  • Give each age group only its own feed, as your supervisor tells you.
  • Never give mouldy, wet or bad-smelling feed.
  • Store feed dry, off the floor, first in first out.
  • Never climb into a feed silo.
  • Record feed used and report a drop in eating.
